coupled/iphone13/ch02-search-end.jpg.title: Finding the promoter
coupled/iphone13/ch02-search-end.jpg.caption: RNA polymerase holoenzyme scans the DNA. Its σ⁷⁰ subunit (violet) recognises the −35 TTGACA and −10 TATAAT promoter elements.

coupled/iphone13/ch03-open-end.jpg.title: Opening the DNA
coupled/iphone13/ch03-open-end.jpg.caption: σ⁷⁰ melts about 13 base pairs around the start site. The template strand enters the active site and the DNA bends sharply.

coupled/iphone13/ch04-initiate-end.jpg.title: First bonds
coupled/iphone13/ch04-initiate-end.jpg.caption: Each incoming NTP pairs with the template. The RNA 3′-OH attacks its α-phosphate, adding one nucleotide and releasing pyrophosphate.

coupled/iphone13/ch05-escape-end.jpg.caption: After about 12 nucleotides the enzyme leaves the promoter. Here σ⁷⁰ is shown leaving; in cells it often stays bound for longer.
